en.title: Frameset vs complete bike: what does a build really cost?
en.description: Compare complete-bike prices with frame-plus-parts budgets. A worked INCOLOR Voyager example shows included parts, a known subtotal and costs still to quote.
en.intro: Compare the cost of a bike you can ride: the frame package, every missing part, assembly and delivery. A frameset can make sense when you want a specific fit or build, but its sticker price cannot tell you whether it saves money. Start with an allowance, then replace it with an itemized budget.

sections.heading: Compare rideable totals first
paragraphs: A bargain frame has a talent for inviting expensive friends. The catalog adds a reviewed remaining-build allowance to each recorded frame price, so a bare frame does not appear cheaper simply because it is missing most of a bicycle. The total is a shortlist estimate, not a shop quote.

The [itemized builder](/build/) serves a different purpose: choose an exact base and component slots, then inspect what is known and what is missing. A known subtotal is not a complete budget while required slots, prices or compatibility information are unresolved.

sections.heading: A worked budget: frame, groupset… and the rest
paragraphs: Begin with the seller’s exact option name. Does it include the fork, headset, through-axles, seatpost, cockpit, hanger and small hardware? Are brakes included with a shifting package? Mark included parts once; do not add the same component again in another slot.

Then list the remaining drivetrain, brakes and rotors, wheels, tires, tubes or tubeless supplies, contact points, pedals and assembly work as applicable. Confirm what the mechanic’s quote includes. The objective is not to assume every build needs the same shopping list, but to make each omission explicit.

Here is a cost sketch using the INCOLOR Voyager starting price and a recorded Shimano 105 Di2 large package. The package already covers several parts; counting its brakes, crankset, cassette or chain again would inflate the total. The unpriced rows are where the budget still needs work.

sections.heading: A cheap part that does not fit is not a saving
paragraphs: Check the recorded frame interfaces against the chosen components: bottom bracket and crank spindle, brake mount and rotor setup, axle dimensions, freehub and cassette, hanger and derailleur, and any cockpit or seatpost restrictions. Unknowns remain questions, not automatic passes.

The builder flags only constraints represented in the dataset. It does not inspect physical parts, guarantee compatibility or replace the manufacturer’s installation instructions. Share the actual component list with the person who will assemble the bike before purchasing.

sections.heading: When does a self-build make sense?
paragraphs: Put the completed worksheet beside a specific complete-bike configuration. Keep the fit, tire requirement, drivetrain layout and wheel choice visible. A lighter or more expensive wheelset in the self-build means the two budgets no longer describe the same outcome.

Also separate one-time build cost from support. Ask who handles a frame problem, a drivetrain problem and an assembly problem, and how shipping or workshop labor is treated. Do not assume that buying all components separately produces one unified warranty.
bullets: Choose a complete bike when its actual configuration meets your needs and its delivered quote beats your finished build budget.
Choose a frameset when the fit, frame features or component choices justify the complete cost and the assembly work.
If you already own usable parts, list them explicitly and check compatibility; only then remove their purchase cost from the budget.

sections.heading: Turn the sketch into your own build
paragraphs: Save the date and conditions with each quote so you can return to the same configuration when it is time to order.

Open a [Voyager build plan](/build/?base=incolor-voyager-frameset) or an [LCG071S-PRO build plan](/build/?base=lightcarbon-lcg071s-pro-frameset), replace the missing prices with quotes, and compare the result with the [Twitter complete bike](/models/twitter-v3-wheeltop-eds/). Keep unknown costs blank until you have an answer. The total should help you decide, not merely look finished.

zh-Hans.title: 买车架还是整车？算清一辆能骑的车要多少钱
zh-Hans.description: 用车架、配件和装配费用比较整车价格。以 INCOLOR Voyager 为例，列出已包含配件、已知小计与仍待报价的项目。
zh-Hans.intro: 比较的应是一辆能骑的车：车架套餐、缺少的配件、装配和运费都要算进去。想要特定几何或配置时，自组车很有吸引力，但车架标价本身不能说明是否省钱。先用装车预算筛选，再用逐项报价替换。

sections.heading: 先比一辆能骑的车，总共要多少
paragraphs: 便宜车架很会“交朋友”：轮组、套件和小配件很快就来报到了。目录在车架价格上加一笔已复核的装车预算，避免一套缺了大半辆车的车架只因标价低而显得便宜。这个总额适合筛选，不是车店报价。
[逐项装车工具](/build/)用于选择具体基础车型与各部件，再检查已知和缺失信息。只要必需槽位、价格或兼容性仍未确定，“已知小计”就不是完整预算。

sections.heading: 算一遍：车架、大套，以及剩下的项目
paragraphs: 从卖家的准确选项名称开始：是否包含前叉、碗组、桶轴、座管、把组、尾钩及小配件？变速套餐是否已包含刹车？内含部件只计算一次，不能又在其他槽位重复加价。
然后按实际需要列出剩余变速、刹车与碟片、轮组、轮胎、内胎或真空胎耗材、接触部件、脚踏及装配费用，并确认车店报价的范围。目的不是假设每辆车都需要同一份购物清单，而是把遗漏写出来。
下面用 INCOLOR Voyager 起价和已记录的 Shimano 105 Di2 大套做费用示例。大套已经覆盖若干项目，再单独加一次刹车、牙盘、飞轮或链条，就重复计费了。尚未报价的行，才是接下来要补齐的预算。

sections.heading: 不兼容的便宜配件不是省钱
paragraphs: 逐项核对已记录接口与所选配件：中轴及曲柄轴心、刹车座与碟片、桶轴尺寸、塔基与飞轮、尾钩与后拨，以及把组、座管的限制。未知项是问题，不是自动通过。
配置器只能提示数据中已记录的约束，不会检查实物，也不保证兼容性或取代厂家的安装说明。购买前，把具体配件单交给实际负责装车的人确认。

sections.heading: 什么情况下，自组车更值得？
paragraphs: 把完整清单与一个具体整车配置并排比较，保留合身、轮胎、单双盘和轮组选择。自组方案用了更轻或更贵的轮组，两份预算就不再对应同样的结果。
还要把一次性装车成本与售后分开。问清车架、变速与装配问题分别由谁负责，运费和工时如何处理。分别购买所有部件，不代表最终会得到统一保修。
bullets: 整车实际配置符合需求，且含运费报价低于完成后的自组预算，可以优先考虑整车。
车架的几何、功能或配件选择足以支持完整预算与装配投入时，再考虑自组。
已有可用配件时，先逐项列出并确认兼容，再从购买预算中扣除对应成本。

sections.heading: 把示例变成自己的装车单
paragraphs: 把日期和条件与每份报价一起保存，准备下单时，才能找到当时确认的同一配置。

打开 [Voyager 装车方案](/build/?base=incolor-voyager-frameset)或 [LCG071S-PRO 装车方案](/build/?base=lightcarbon-lcg071s-pro-frameset)，用实际报价补齐缺少的价格，再与[骓特整车](/models/twitter-v3-wheeltop-eds/)比较。未确认费用先留空；总价应当帮助作决定，而不是看起来已经算完。
